worlds.interpretation: decision-level allowed set is exact, but the preregistered exact-prime-interface endpoint fails because the frozen candidate basis retains 125 additional clauses

worlds.claim: The byte-frozen k=4 derivation grammar is incomplete on this unseen world. This is a counterexample to universal exactness of the frozen R12B k=4 compiler, not a proof that no other polynomial representation or algorithm exists.

worlds.interpretation: semantic UNSAT interface is exact, but the frozen prime-geometry scoring representation disagrees with the one-empty-clause minimal contradiction representation; this remains OPEN under the preregistered endpoint and is not retroactively repaired

scientific_update.exactness: Three of six unseen worlds pass both exact allowed-set and exact-prime-interface endpoints. Two additional worlds preserve the exact allowed set but fail the frozen interface-structure endpoint. One unseen planted n=40 world produces five false-positive bridge assignments under the frozen k=4 compiler.
scientific_update.width: R13-W05 is the decisive killer-test result: the frozen k=4 quotient compiler reached a proof-replayable fixed point without creating width>4 states, yet missed 14 exact prime implicates and admitted five assignments that the exact witness rejects. The recorded missing implicates include width-5 and width-6 clauses.
scientific_update.soundness: No false negatives were observed in any scored world. Proof replay and compiler firewall passed; the observed R13-W05 failure is incompleteness of the frozen candidate grammar, not an observed unsound derivation.
scientific_update.scaling: The 24/32/40 ladder is exploratory only. Pair attempts range from 0.39M to 47.17M and the normalized work is highly instance-dependent. No global polynomial runtime envelope is established.

state_universe_statement: N_4(n)=SUM_{i=0..4} binom(n,i)2^i=O(n^4) remains true for the frozen state representation, but R13 demonstrates that a polynomial-sized k=4 state universe is not sufficient for universal exactness of this compiler.
next_gate_requirements: Freeze R12B and R13 artifacts unchanged.
Treat R13-W05 as a preserved counterexample, not a tuning example for R12B.
Determine whether the five false-positive assignments can be separated by a minimal prospective extension whose representation contract is frozen before testing new worlds.
Distinguish required intermediate derivation width from final interface clause width and from alternative representations with auxiliaries.
Separately resolve the R13-W04/W06 interface-representation mismatch without changing the already scored R13 verdict.
claim_ceiling: R13 falsifies universal exactness of the frozen R12B k=4 quotient compiler on the frozen unseen test set. It does not establish P!=NP, does not establish that width>4 is necessary for every exact representation, and does not rule out another polynomial algorithm.
seal: THE UNSEEN WORLD DID BREAK THE FROZEN COMPILER. THAT IS THE RESULT WE WANTED THE CONTROL TO BE ABLE TO PRODUCE. KEEP THE THREE PASSES, KEEP THE TWO STRUCTURE MISMATCHES, KEEP THE FIVE FALSE POSITIVES, AND DO NOT MOVE K AFTER THE FACT.
